To configure scalar relativistic DFT for transition metal clusters in ORCA, use the 'ZORA' or 'DKH' keywords in the simple input line (e.g., '! PBE ZORA'). It is mandatory to use relativistically recontracted basis sets, such as 'ZORA-def2-TZVP' or the 'SARC-ZORA-TZVP' series for heavy elements beyond Krypton. For SARC basis sets, always specify the 'SARC/J' auxiliary basis. For core properties like XAS, ensure the relativistic picture change is accounted for by adding:
%rel
  Method ZORA
  PictureChange true
end
Example: ! PBE ZORA SARC-ZORA-TZVP SARC/J Opt

For reliable geometry optimizations of transition metal complexes, use '! TightSCF' to minimize numerical noise in gradients. Integration grids should be high quality, typically '! Grid4' or '! Grid5'; the 'NoFinalGrid' option is often recommended to maintain consistency throughout the optimization. For heavy metal centers, increase radial integration accuracy to avoid 'noise' in the SCF by setting:
%scf
  intacc 9.0
end
If convergence is unstable, you can use the SOSCF helper:
%scf
  SOSCFStart 0.01
  CNVSOSCF true
end

To perform XAS calculations in ORCA (often following or during a geometry optimization), use TD-DFT or PNO-ROCIS. For TD-DFT, use the '%tddft' block to define the number of roots (e.g., '%tddft NRoots 50 end'). For more efficient linear-scaling core excitations, use PNO-ROCIS:
%rocis
  DoPNO true
  TCutPNO 1e-11
  XASElems <atom_index>
  OrbWin = 0,0,0,<n_core_orbs>
end
Note that 'XASElems' identifies the target element by its zero-based index in the coordinate list, and 'OrbWin' restricts the excitation space to core orbitals. For L-edge spectra, ensure spin-orbit coupling is included via '%rel DoSOC true end'.
